stem.text: Let \( f(x) = \frac{4 x^{2}}{x^{3} + 3} \) and \( a_n = f(n) \). State the conditions the integral test requires for the series \( \sum_{n=2}^{\infty} a_n \), and use the test to determine whether the series converges or diverges.

answer_key.label: \( \sum a_n \) diverges, because f is positive, decreasing and continuous on \( [2, \infty) \) and \( \lim_{b\to\infty} \int_{2}^{b} f(x)\,dx = \infty \).

worked_solution.text: On \( [2, \infty) \), f is positive, continuous because \( x^{3} + 3 \) is positive there, and decreasing because \( f^{\prime}(x) = - \frac{4 x \left(x^{3} - 6\right)}{\left(x^{3} + 3\right)^{2}} \) is negative there.

\( \lim_{b\to\infty} \left[\frac{4 \ln{\left(x^{3} + 3 \right)}}{3}\right]_{2}^{b} = \lim_{b\to\infty} \left(\frac{4 \ln{\left(b^{3} + 3 \right)}}{3} - \left(\frac{4 \ln{\left(11 \right)}}{3}\right)\right) \), and the first term approaches \( \infty \), so \( \lim_{b\to\infty} \int_{2}^{b} f(x)\,dx = \infty \).
worked_solution.rule_named: limit notation on an improper integral

worked_solution.text: The integral diverges, so by the integral test \( \sum_{n=2}^{\infty} a_n \) diverges.
